core_obligations: Translate the diagram (proof lines 780-800): the correspondence groups from a scheme to the base are cycle groups, and composing with a correspondence is pullback of cycles; the lemma describing the correspondence of a graph converts this into the usual pushforward and pullback of cycles, so the two routes around the diagram become two expressions which are to be compared.

Compute both routes (proof lines 800-815): pulling back the fundamental cycle of the product along the second factor and then along the graph correspondence gives the pushforward of the diagonal, which is the graph of the morphism; going the other way, pulling back the fundamental cycle of the product along the first factor and then along the transpose correspondence gives the Gysin pullback of the diagonal along the graph, which is again the graph of the morphism by the computation of the Gysin pullback of the diagonal.
Conclude (proof lines 815-827): both routes produce the element of the correspondence group between the products corresponding to the cycle of the graph, so the diagram commutes.
proof_roadmap: Translate the diagram into pullbacks of fundamental cycles using the correspondence of graphs.
Compute both routes and identify the results with the graph of the morphism.
Conclude the commutativity of the diagram.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves the commutativity of a square and triangle diagram built from the graph correspondence, its transpose, the diagonal correspondences and the fundamental classes of two equidimensional smooth projective schemes (statement lines 776-793). The proof (proof lines 794-827) translates the diagram into two pullbacks of fundamental cycles, computes both routes using the description of correspondences of graphs, and identifies both with the graph of the morphism. H3: a diagram chase carried out in full.
